description: Bound dead-worker re-dispatch in the sentinel loop with escalating backoff + a retry cap, mirroring the no-progress guard, so a persistently dying worker blocks cleanly instead of storming to MAX_ITERATIONS.

userStories.title: Escalating backoff + retry cap for dead-pane outcomes in the sentinel loop
userStories.description: As the supervisor, when a worker dies pre-result (pane-died) or times out, I need to back off with an escalating delay and stop after a bounded number of consecutive failures, instead of immediately re-dispatching and burning MAX_ITERATIONS in a storm.
acceptanceCriteria: src/supervisor/loop.ts exports MAX_DEAD_WORKER_RETRIES = 3 (mirroring MAX_NO_PROGRESS_RETRIES) and reuses NO_PROGRESS_BACKOFF_MS for the delay.
A deadWorkerStreak counter is incremented on pollOutcome 'pane-died' OR 'timeout'.

When deadWorkerStreak >= MAX_DEAD_WORKER_RETRIES, the loop calls notifyTerminal('blocked') and returns { status: 'blocked', iterations, lastOutcome } without dispatching again (never reaches MAX_ITERATIONS).

Below the cap, the loop emits a 'pane-died-retry' event with detail { attempt: deadWorkerStreak, backoffMs: NO_PROGRESS_BACKOFF_MS * deadWorkerStreak, pollOutcome } and calls sleepFn(NO_PROGRESS_BACKOFF_MS * deadWorkerStreak) before continuing to the next dispatch.

deadWorkerStreak resets to 0 at every point where noProgressStreak resets (the sentinel-success paths AND the review-branch reset at the end of a review iteration), so a transient pane-death followed by ANY real loop progress does not block.
The timeout branch keeps respawning the pane with the existing 'echo timeout' command before backing off.
'pane-died-retry' is added to the WorkerEventKind union in src/supervisor/events.ts (closed union; typecheck would fail otherwise).

Test: with isPaneAlive returning false persistently, the loop performs at most MAX_DEAD_WORKER_RETRIES dispatches with escalating sleepFn calls (NO_PROGRESS_BACKOFF_MS then 2*NO_PROGRESS_BACKOFF_MS), emits a 'pane-died-retry' before each retry, and returns status 'blocked' (never 'max-iterations').
Test: a transient pane-death (one) followed by a live pane that yields a DONE sentinel does not block and resets the streak.
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/loop.ts (sentinel branch around lines 518-559: the pane-died branch ~543 and the timeout branch ~551), src/supervisor/events.ts (WorkerEventKind union ~51), test/supervisor/loop.test.ts (makeBaseOpts injects isPaneAlive/sleepFn/nowMs; donePane(storyId) yields the sentinel pane text). Mirror the existing CAM-36/38 no-progress guard pattern (streak increment, cap -> notifyTerminal('blocked')+return, else emit retry event + sleepFn). Reuse NO_PROGRESS_BACKOFF_MS; do NOT add a separate backoff const. Reset deadWorkerStreak on the successful-sentinel path (where readWorkerOutcome runs), next to where noProgressStreak semantics live.

userStories.title: Doc-sync the bounded dead-worker retry in the recovery runbook
userStories.description: As a future operator, I need the recovery runbook to reflect that dead-worker re-dispatch is now bounded and to list the new event so the diagnostics section stays accurate.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/recovery-runbook.md scenario (f) 'Diagnosing with the event log' lists the 'pane-died-retry' event kind with a one-line description (grep -q 'pane-died-retry' docs/recovery-runbook.md returns 0).
The dead-pane recovery scenarios note the bounded re-dispatch capped at MAX_DEAD_WORKER_RETRIES (grep -q 'MAX_DEAD_WORKER_RETRIES' docs/recovery-runbook.md returns 0).
No em-dash appears in the edited markdown (use colon, comma, parens, or period).
userStories.notes: Files: docs/recovery-runbook.md. The event-log diagnostics section already enumerates emitted event kinds (worker-start, worker-end, result, tokens, pushed, stale-lock); add 'pane-died-retry'. Depends on US-001 having added the event. No source change in this story.

docsConsultedRationale: No external library touched: internal supervisor state-machine guard + existing WorkerEventKind union (closed) + markdown doc only.
